test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-2) Official Paper (Held On: 13 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the full form of SJSRY in relation to self-employment programmes implemented by the Government of India in 1997?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **On December 1st, 1997, the Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) **programme was implemented in **India**.
 
• The programme encourages the creation of self-employment projects or the provision of pay employment in an effort to give the underemployed and the poor in metropolitan areas to access to productive employment.
 
• Cost-sharing between the Center and the States in the ratio of **75:25** is being used to implement the **SJSRY system.**
 
• Only 50,000 urban poor people receive benefits under** SJSRY,** **self-employment **due to the inadequate allocations for the programme, which benefits roughly 2 lakh urban poor people under skill development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Considering that the number of the urban poor was predicted to be** 81 million in 2004–2005 and that the Nationwide Council on Skill Development **has set a national aim of 500 million people to be skill-trained by 2022, the target under skill development for the urban poor is quite low.
 
• **The SJSRY was discontinued in 2013** in favour of the National Urban Livelihood Mission (NULM), which is now known as the** Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM).**
 
• Both are merely job programmes designed to let urban poor people work for themselves and for pay. For urban areas, there is no MGNREGA-style employment guarantee programme as of 2022.
